question: What is the main purpose of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA)?

options.A: To assign blame and punishment to negligent staff members
options.B: To calculate the financial cost of patient lawsuits
options.C: To investigate why an error occurred by identifying underlying system flaws
options.D: To evaluate the daily bedside performance of individual students

explanation: RCA is like detective work! It looks deep into the system to find out why a mistake happened, rather than just pointing fingers at a person.

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: Ensuring no harm comes to the patient or nurse during the procedure
options.B: Reducing the overall cost of purchasing hospital medical supplies
options.C: Speeding up the time it takes to administer daily medication rounds
options.D: Eliminating the need to wear gloves when handling clean syringes

explanation: Injection safety focuses entirely on protecting both recipients and healthcare providers from physical harm and infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the most effective nursing action when supporting stressed parents of a newly diagnosed child?

options.A: Focus only on the child and ignore parental emotional health
options.B: Tell them to stop worrying because children always outgrow it
options.C: Connect them with local parent support groups and active listening
options.D: Advise them to change schools immediately without investigation

explanation: Emotional support and peer connections help parents cope with the challenges of navigating a new diagnosis. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h7)

question: Why are straps fastened across the chest, hips, and knees during ambulance transport?

options.A: To increase blood flow directly back to the heart chambers
options.B: To stop the patient from talking too loudly to the driver
options.C: To keep the patient completely awake throughout the journey
options.D: To prevent the patient from sliding or falling during sharp turns

explanation: Ambulances make sudden turns and stops, making secure strapping vital to keep the patient safe on the stretcher. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why would a doctor prescribe corticosteroids for a patient suffering from severe serum sickness?

options.A: To replace missing complement proteins in the bloodstream
options.B: To quickly reduce widespread inflammation and immune activity
options.C: To kill any underlying bacterial infection in the skin
options.D: To permanently destroy the patient's antibody-producing cells

explanation: Corticosteroids act like a calming balm for the overactive immune system, easing the pain and swelling.

question: What is a major risk when a country relies too heavily on international aid for its health care?

options.A: Aid can be unpredictable and subject to changes in donor priorities
options.B: It automatically guarantees universal health coverage for all citizens
options.C: It forces the government to increase local tax rates every month
options.D: It eliminates out-of-pocket spending across all private hospitals

explanation: External funding can shift based on foreign politics, meaning sudden withdrawals can collapse local programs. Building self-reliance is always better!

question: Why are nurses often referred to as the final safety net in clinical care?

options.A: They write all the hospital safety policies and clinical guidelines
options.B: They pay for any financial penalties resulting from medical mistakes
options.C: They have the legal authority to fire negligent doctors
options.D: They are the last healthcare workers to catch errors before harm occurs

explanation: Because nurses spend the most continuous time at the bedside, they are uniquely positioned to double-check orders and catch mistakes right before they affect the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why do hydatid cysts often go unnoticed for a long time after infection?

options.A: They dissolve quickly inside the bloodstream
options.B: They grow very slowly over months or years
options.C: They immediately trigger severe immune rejection
options.D: They only affect areas with no nerve supply

explanation: Because these cysts grow so slowly, they stay quiet and hidden for a long time before crowding nearby organs.

question: A patient with a chronic illness stops taking their routine medicines because they can no longer afford cash payments. What is this financial challenge called?

options.A: Over-insurance by the federal scheme
options.B: Mandatory prepayment taxation
options.C: Catastrophic out-of-pocket expenditure
options.D: Excessive foreign donor funding

explanation: Spot on! Paying cash directly for chronic medical care quickly drains family savings, forcing many patients to abandon their treatment.

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for teaching a patient with an endocrine condition?

options.A: Providing clear written action plans for emergency symptoms
options.B: Tailoring the teaching session to the patient's cultural background
options.C: Giving long medical lectures without checking for understanding
options.D: Using a return-demonstration approach for practical skills

explanation: Correct! Long, boring lectures don't help anyone learn. We always want interactive teaching and plenty of feedback!

question: Why might a patient feel surprisingly little pain right after a very severe full-thickness burn?

options.A: The outer skin layer blocks the pain signals from traveling
options.B: Deep muscle tissue absorbs all the initial heat energy
options.C: The body releases a large amount of natural painkillers
options.D: The nerve endings in the skin have been destroyed

explanation: Spot on! Because full-thickness burns destroy the skin completely, the nerve endings that usually send pain signals to the brain are burnt away.

question: What does a flashing red light or a chirping sound on an AED usually mean?

options.A: The AED battery is fully charged and ready for an emergency.
options.B: The device has failed a self-test and requires attention.
options.C: The electrode pads are currently connected to a patient.
options.D: The machine is downloading software updates from the hospital.

explanation: That little red light or chirp is your friendly warning that the AED needs a check-up—maybe a new battery or fresh pads—so it's ready when needed.

question: Which type of medication is usually prescribed to help strengthen bones in patients with osteoporosis?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Bisphosphonates
options.C: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.D: Sedative hypnotics

explanation: Bisphosphonates act like a brake on bone breakdown, helping the body hold onto its bone density.

question: What is the primary purpose of an adult day care home?

options.A: To offer permanent residential housing for older adults
options.B: To serve as a 24-hour acute care hospital ward
options.C: To provide specialized surgical interventions
options.D: To provide daytime supervised care and support services

explanation: Adult day care homes are specifically designed to offer structured programs, supervision, and support during daytime hours while allowing clients to return home at night. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which clinical sign suggests that a newborn with a skull injury may have underlying intracranial pressure?

options.A: A strong grip reflex in both hands
options.B: Rapid passage of meconium stool
options.C: A high-pitched cry and lethargy
options.D: An intense craving for frequent feeds

explanation: Neurological irritability, altered levels of consciousness like lethargy, and a high-pitched cry are classic indicators of increased pressure inside the cranium. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h4)

question: What protective layer of cells surrounds a secondary oocyte when it is released during ovulation?

options.A: Myometrium lining
options.B: Endometrial stroma
options.C: Amniotic membrane
options.D: Corona radiata

explanation: The corona radiata is a supportive halo of follicular cells wrapped around the egg that incoming sperm must work through during fertilization.

question: Why is it dangerous to give sugary drinks to an unconscious patient with low blood sugar?

options.A: The stomach will reject all sugary liquids
options.B: It can cause choking or enter the lungs
options.C: It will immediately cause a diabetic coma
options.D: It takes three days for the body to digest it

explanation: An unconscious patient cannot protect their airway. Giving them fluids by mouth can cause aspiration, sending liquid straight into their lungs. Safety first!

question: Why do health programs often fail if nurses ignore local cultural values?

options.A: Because government laws forbid treating people with different beliefs
options.B: Because the community feels disrespected and rejects outside interference
options.C: Because local leaders charge heavy fines for unapproved advice
options.D: Because medications lose their chemical potency in different cultures

explanation: Always respect local culture! When people feel understood and respected, they are much more likely to welcome healthcare programs.

question: Which factor represents part of the physical school health environment?

options.A: Safe water supply and clean toilets
options.B: The political climate of the community
options.C: The emotional stability of the principal
options.D: The grading system used for examinations

explanation: Physical components refer to tangible structures and amenities like safe drinking water, ventilation, and sanitation facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: How does community participation influence the success of a primary health care program?

options.A: It ensures the community accepts and sustains the health interventions
options.B: It guarantees that every resident becomes a trained community health worker
options.C: It removes the need for government funding of local health posts
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all administrative duties to villagers

explanation: When people help plan their own health programs, they take ownership and support them long-term. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is preventable harm in healthcare?

options.A: Allergic reactions to drugs with no prior history of allergy
options.B: Unavoidable side effects of a necessary surgical operation
options.C: Natural progression of a terminal disease without treatment
options.D: Damage caused by failing to follow accepted standards of care

explanation: Preventable harm is injury that could have been avoided if standard safety practices were properly followed. Every check we do counts!

question: A patient cries out with sharp, shooting pain down their leg while receiving an IM injection in the buttocks. What has most likely happened?

options.A: The needle has irritated or hit the sciatic nerve
options.B: The muscle is experiencing a normal cramp
options.C: The needle gauge is too small for the fluid
options.D: The medication is reacting with subcutaneous fat

explanation: Shooting pain down the leg is a classic sign of nerve trauma, specifically involving the sciatic nerve during poor dorsogluteal injections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do quantitative researchers try to remain completely neutral and detached from their study participants?

options.A: To avoid having to write detailed nursing care plans
options.B: To prevent personal bias from affecting the study results
options.C: To make it easier to recruit busy hospital staff
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of running the project

explanation: Staying objective ensures the data truly reflects reality, rather than what the researcher hopes or wishes to see.

question: What is the main reason paracetamol (acetaminophen) is different from a true NSAID?

options.A: It causes severe stomach ulcers within hours of use
options.B: It can only be given through intravenous injection
options.C: It completely blocks both COX-1 and COX-2 permanently
options.D: It lacks significant anti-inflammatory properties

explanation: Paracetamol is great for knocking out a fever or a headache, but it doesn't do much for swelling or joint inflammation like ibuprofen does. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the main trigger that causes ovulation to happen?

options.A: A rapid drop in circulating estrogen levels
options.B: A constant high level of progesterone
options.C: A sudden, sharp surge of Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
options.D: A steady rise in basal body temperature

explanation: Boom! That mid-cycle spike in Luteinizing Hormone (the LH surge) is what weakens the ovarian wall and lets the mature egg pop out.

question: What makes adaptive immunity so special compared to innate immunity?

options.A: It relies entirely on physical barriers like unbroken skin layers
options.B: It responds instantly within the first few minutes of exposure
options.C: It creates specific immunological memory against specific pathogens
options.D: It requires no cellular coordination or chemical signaling

explanation: Spot on! Adaptive immunity never forgets. Once it fights a germ, it remembers it, so if that same germ attacks later, your body fights back much faster and stronger.

question: Why is high potassium (hyperkalemia) considered so dangerous to patient safety?

options.A: It melts the protective coating on nerves
options.B: It can cause fatal changes in heart rhythm
options.C: It causes severe bone fractures
options.D: It immediately stops the lungs from breathing

explanation: Potassium directly controls the electrical activity of the heart muscle, so high levels easily trigger lethal heart rhythms. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is generally safe and does NOT harm sperm production?

options.A: Regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Anabolic steroid abuse
options.C: Elevated scrotal temperature
options.D: Exposure to heavy toxins

explanation: Good news! Regular, moderate exercise keeps your body healthy and balanced. Heat, harsh toxins, and steroids, however, can hurt sperm counts.

question: What is Chadwick's sign?

options.A: A bluish discoloration of the vagina and cervix
options.B: A softening of the lower uterine segment
options.C: The fluttering sensation of fetal movement
options.D: A softening of service tip

explanation: Chadwick's sign is that distinct bluish-violet tint in the vaginal walls caused by extra blood rushing to the area during pregnancy.

question: Why is it important for the body to release hormones in pulses?

options.A: It ensures constant, unvarying blood pressure all day
options.B: It prevents receptor down-regulation and desensitization
options.C: It stops the nervous system from sending electrical signals
options.D: It triggers immediate humoral stimulation in the pancreas

explanation: If cells are flooded with hormones non-stop, they get 'numb' to them. Pulsing keeps the cell receptors fresh and listening!

question: Which of the following is NOT a common physical complication of severe, prolonged vomiting in pregnancy?

options.A: Electrolyte and acid-base imbalance
options.B: Esophageal tears from forceful retching
options.C: Acute kidney injury from dehydration
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Gestational diabetes is related to insulin resistance and glucose metabolism, not directly caused by vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h6)

question: How can occupational health nurses make sure their safety training is actually effective for all workers?

options.A: By adapting training materials to be simple, practical, and easy to understand
options.B: By using highly complex medical textbooks that require a university degree to read
options.C: By handing out written instructions in languages the workers cannot speak
options.D: By only training company managers and ignoring junior floor workers

explanation: Good teaching meets people where they are. Using simple, relatable language ensures every single worker understands how to stay safe.

question: What veterinary practice is key to stopping the spread of hydatid disease?

options.A: Preventing dogs from eating raw livestock offal
options.B: Isolating newborn calves from adult animals
options.C: Dipping cattle in chemical insecticides weekly
options.D: Vaccinating all sheep against bacterial infections

explanation: Stopping dogs from eating infected animal parts at slaughterhouses breaks the tapeworm cycle completely.

question: How do pelvic adhesions and scar tissue lead to trouble getting pregnant?

options.A: They cause the uterus to completely shed its lining every week
options.B: They can physically block the normal path of eggs through the fallopian tubes
options.C: They destroy all circulating estrogen in the bloodstream
options.D: They prevent the pituitary gland from releasing luteinizing hormone

explanation: Think of scar tissue as web-like knots that twist and block the fallopian tubes, making it hard for the egg and sperm to meet up.

question: You just finished changing a wound dressing and took off your soiled gloves. What should you do next?

options.A: Dispose of the soiled dressing tray in the general waste bin
options.B: Write the nursing notes in the chart while walking to the sink
options.C: Perform hand hygiene immediately before touching anything else
options.D: Put on a fresh pair of clean gloves to tidy up the bedside table

explanation: Microbes can sneak through tiny microscopic tears in gloves. Always clean your hands right after taking them off to stay safe!

question: What goes wrong when a manager only treats the surface symptoms of a ward problem?

options.A: Hospital management will immediately fire the nursing staff
options.B: The budget for the ward will be permanently frozen
options.C: The underlying issue remains and will happen again
options.D: Patients will stop coming to the clinic entirely

explanation: Just scratching the surface leaves the root cause untouched. Until you fix the core issue, the exact same problem is bound to return.

question: How should a nurse balance medical technology use with the developmental needs of a toddler?

options.A: By keeping the child sedated so they do not disturb the machine
options.B: By arranging equipment and tubing to allow safe, supervised play
options.C: By focusing entirely on the machine settings and ignoring play
options.D: By removing all medical devices whenever the child wants to play

explanation: Well done! Toddlers need to move and explore to grow, so helping families organize equipment keeps them safe while still letting them play. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to understand cultural and religious food rules during a nutritional assessment?

options.A: It proves whether the patient has an undiagnosed metabolic enzyme defect
options.B: It replaces the need for standard anthropometric and biochemical testing
options.C: It allows the nurse to legally mandate changes in traditional cooking methods
options.D: It helps the nurse design realistic and culturally acceptable dietary plans

explanation: Diet advice won't work if it ignores what the patient's culture or religion allows them to eat. Meeting patients where they are is key!

question: What makes the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) so great for massive community campaigns?

options.A: It is given through an injection that leaves a lasting scar
options.B: It contains live bacteria that cure existing paralysis
options.C: It does not require any temperature control or refrigeration
options.D: It is simple to administer and builds good gut immunity

explanation: Brilliant! Drops are easy to give without needing injection pros, and they build strong defense right where the virus enters—the gut.

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks suddenly experiences painless vaginal bleeding. What condition should immediately come to mind?

options.A: Preeclampsia
options.B: Placenta previa
options.C: Placental abruption
options.D: Uterine rupture

explanation: A classic clinical clue! Bright red, painless bleeding in the late second or third trimester is the textbook sign of placenta previa.

question: Why does public stigma surrounding mental illness often hurt patients?

options.A: It improves community support networks for families
options.B: It guarantees immediate admission to a general ward
options.C: It automatically lowers the patient's blood pressure
options.D: It delays seeking professional medical treatment

explanation: Stigma and fear of being judged often cause families to hide loved ones or turn only to traditional options first, delaying the proper medical help they deserve.

question: Why is reproductive health nursing considered a sensitive area of care?

options.A: It involves more paperwork than other clinical departments
options.B: It deals with deeply personal aspects tied to self-image and culture
options.C: Medical treatments for these conditions are always experimental
options.D: Patients are rarely willing to talk about their symptoms

explanation: Exactly! Reproductive health touches on private parts of life, culture, and identity. Showing extra empathy and privacy goes a long way.

question: Which sign indicates that a patient is developing contrast-induced nephropathy days after an IVP?

options.A: A temporary metallic taste in the mouth
options.B: A sudden rash appearing on the chest
options.C: A delayed rise in serum creatinine levels
options.D: A mild episode of dizziness right after standing

explanation: Kidney injury from contrast dye typically shows up as an abnormal elevation in blood creatinine levels within two days of the test. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when treating young children with HIV?

options.A: Calculating doses carefully according to the child's exact weight
options.B: Using dispersible or pleasant-tasting liquid formulations
options.C: Involving caregivers closely in daily medication administration
options.D: Using standard adult high-dose tablets without breaking them

explanation: Correct! Adult tablets are not safe or accurate for kids. Children need syrups, dispersible tablets, and exact weight-based dosing.

question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands lack ducts and secrete straight into the blood
options.B: Endocrine glands release sweat and digestive enzymes onto body surfaces
options.C: Exocrine glands use rich capillary networks instead of tubular ducts
options.D: Exocrine glands produce chemical messengers for distant target organs

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as being ductless—they pour their chemical messages directly into the bloodstream. Exocrine glands, like sweat glands, use tubes (ducts) to send their products to a body surface. You've got this!

question: What happens if a learning activity doesn't match what you are actually supposed to learn?

options.A: Instructors no longer need to write lesson plans
options.B: The student automatically passes the nursing board examination
options.C: The clinical ward becomes much cleaner and organized
options.D: Student confusion occurs and assessments lose their validity

explanation: If you are tested on things you never really practiced, it leads to confusion and unfair testing. Good alignment keeps things clear!

question: What is your immediate action if the patient feels sharp pain while you are flushing their ear?

options.A: Push the syringe faster to clear the blockage
options.B: Lower the temperature of the water
options.C: Stop the irrigation procedure right away
options.D: Ask the patient to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Pain is a warning sign of injury! Stop immediately to protect your patient from further harm. You're doing great learning this.

question: What is the biggest drawback of using the mean to summarize patient data?

options.A: It completely ignores the middle values of a normally distributed sample
options.B: It is mathematically impossible to calculate with whole numbers
options.C: It is easily skewed by extreme outlier values in the data set
options.D: It can only be calculated when data is arranged into distinct categories

explanation: Because every single number counts in a mean, a few unusually high or low numbers can pull the average off-center. Good to keep in mind!

question: Why does chronic high blood pressure cause small arteries to permanently narrow over time?

options.A: The heart pumps less blood, causing arteries to shrink from lack of use
options.B: Smooth muscle in the vessel walls thickens in response to the pressure
options.C: Blood clots constantly form and dissolve inside the walls
options.D: Red blood cells stick together and clog the tiny vessels

explanation: Constant high pressure forces the tiny muscles in artery walls to bulk up and thicken, which leaves less open space inside for blood to flow through.

question: Why do we need formal documentation and reports after handling an epidemic?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine daily disease surveillance in hospitals
options.B: It guarantees that the disease will never mutate or return to the country
options.C: It preserves institutional memory and updates national health guidelines
options.D: It allows clinics to bill international agencies for patient treatment meals

explanation: Writing down our experiences leaves a roadmap for future nursing students and health workers to follow. You're doing brilliantly!

question: Why is verifying a patient's identity critical during a tele-nursing consultation?

options.A: To ensure the patient is using an approved brand of mobile phone
options.B: To prevent unauthorized persons from receiving confidential health information
options.C: To confirm that the patient has paid their hospital utility bills
options.D: To make sure the patient's internet connection speed is fast enough

explanation: Identity verification protects patient privacy and ensures sensitive medical details are not disclosed to the wrong party. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: A nurse notices a dark hallway and no grab bars in the shower. What type of assessment is this?

options.A: Home environmental safety assessment
options.B: Pharmacological toxicity review
options.C: Tertiary rehabilitation evaluation
options.D: Secondary disease screening

explanation: Spotting physical risks like poor lighting or missing bathroom grab bars is part of a home environmental safety check.

question: Why should you connect a health topic to the daily life experiences of adult learners?

options.A: Ministry regulations state that lectures must last for at least two hours
options.B: It prevents students from asking difficult questions about medications
options.C: Older individuals cannot memorize new information without a story
options.D: Adults learn best when the topic directly relates to their current life challenges

explanation: Exactly! When learners see how a topic solves their everyday problems, their motivation and memory skyrocket.

question: When nurses are faced with multiple community health problems, which factor helps them decide which to tackle first?

options.A: Color of the local clinic building
options.B: Number of desks in the health office
options.C: Magnitude and severity of the problem
options.D: Personal preference of the junior nurse

explanation: Well done! Problems that affect a lot of people or cause severe illness naturally take top priority in our planning.

question: Which medication is the specific emergency reversal antidote for a heparin overdose?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Naloxone hydrochloride
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Protamine sulfate

explanation: Protamine sulfate is heparin's best counter-punch. It binds right to heparin and neutralizes it almost instantly if bleeding gets out of hand.

question: A ward always has rushed handovers because staff arrive late. What is the best way to fix this?

options.A: Allow outgoing nurses to leave before the incoming shift arrives
options.B: Cancel all shift handovers permanently and rely on text messages
options.C: Reduce the amount of patient care required during the day
options.D: Implement strict arrival policies and use a structured handover checklist

explanation: Using a checklist alongside clear punctuality rules keeps handovers organized, quick, and right on track!

question: What is the main purpose of vocational training programs for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: To train people exclusively for nursing careers
options.B: To provide practical skills for self-reliance and employment
options.C: To keep individuals occupied during long hospital stays
options.D: To replace formal university education entirely

explanation: Vocational training equips individuals with marketable skills so they can earn a living and achieve financial independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h4)

question: How should a nurse respond to a mother who is worried and hesitant about vaccines?

options.A: Tell her that asking questions about health is illegal and disrespectful
options.B: Listen patiently, address her specific worries with facts, and show empathy
options.C: Scold her for neglecting her child and refuse to serve her today
options.D: Ignore her concerns and quickly give the injections without talking

explanation: You've got this! Warm listening and gentle, fact-based guidance are the best ways to ease a parent's worries and build trust.

question: Over time, why does high blood sugar cause damage to organs?

options.A: Sugar molecules directly injure delicate blood vessels and nerves
options.B: Glucose turns into a toxic acid inside major body organs
options.C: The pancreas stops producing all red blood cells
options.D: Extra sugar blocks the normal flow of oxygen to the lungs

explanation: When blood sugar stays high for too long, it acts almost like sandpaper on the tiny, delicate blood vessels and nerves all over the body. Spotting this early helps us protect our patients!

question: You notice rising rates of malnutrition in a local village during your community posting. What is your best first step as a nurse?

options.A: Wait patiently in the health post until parents bring children in
options.B: Demand that international organizations take over food distribution
options.C: Collaborate with local leaders to educate families on using local food sources
options.D: Immediately shut down all local food markets until supplies improve

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders to teach healthy eating using available local foods is practical and sustainable!

question: Which condition is a primary indication for a low salt diet in hospital wards?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Acute bone fractures
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Hypertension is directly linked to sodium intake, making salt restriction a primary medical intervention for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: A patient starts having eclamptic seizures on the ward. What is your very first priority?

options.A: Ask family members to sign consent forms for blood transfusion
options.B: Ensure a clear airway and prepare to administer magnesium sulfate
options.C: Take the patient to the theater immediately for an emergency delivery
options.D: Collect a clean-catch urine sample to check for sugar and protein

explanation: Safety first! Always secure the airway during a seizure, and get magnesium sulfate ready—it's the gold standard drug for stopping eclamptic fits.

question: Which of these best describes permanent harm?

options.A: A temporary drop in blood pressure after changing positions
options.B: A lasting disability or loss of function caused by an error
options.C: A mild headache that resolves after sleeping overnight
options.D: An allergic rash that disappears after taking an antihistamine

explanation: Permanent harm means the patient suffers a long-term or irreversible loss of ability. This is why our daily safety checks are so important.

question: Why would a doctor choose a tracheostomy instead of keeping a breathing tube through the mouth long-term?

options.A: It completely stops any risk of getting an infection
options.B: It means you never have to clean around the site or use suction
options.C: It is much more comfortable and safer for long-term breathing support
options.D: It is much faster to do in an outdoor emergency

explanation: Having a tube taped through the mouth for weeks can damage the vocal cords and mouth. A tracheostomy provides a secure, comfortable airway right through the neck for patients who need long-term help.

question: What usually happens when a clinic doesn't have enough staff according to PHC standards?

options.A: Increased funding from international donor organizations
options.B: Faster turnaround times for routine laboratory investigations
options.C: Elimination of preventable communicable diseases
options.D: Staff burnout and reduced quality of care for patients

explanation: When too few hands carry a heavy load, nurses and staff get exhausted, and patients end up waiting longer or receiving rushed care.

question: Which procedure gives the final, sure diagnosis for uterine cancer?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Urinalysis and culture
options.C: Endometrial biopsy
options.D: Abdominal X-ray

explanation: Spot on! Taking a small tissue sample through a biopsy lets the lab confirm if cancer cells are present.

question: What happens during the McRoberts maneuver when dealing with shoulder dystocia?

options.A: The mother's thighs are flexed sharply toward her abdomen
options.B: The mother is turned completely onto her hands and knees
options.C: Firm pressure is applied directly on top of the mother's fundus
options.D: The nurse pulls gently on the baby's head to release the shoulder

explanation: Pulling her knees right up to her chest changes the pelvis angle and helps pop that stuck shoulder free without pulling on the baby.

question: Which physical sign should a nurse look for when monitoring a patient for worsening heart failure due to severe CAD?

options.A: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles
options.B: Bleeding gums when brushing the teeth
options.C: Sudden uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the eye whites

explanation: When a damaged heart pumps inefficiently, fluid backs up in the body, commonly causing dependent edema in the legs and ankles. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a method of environmental vector control?

options.A: Spraying heavy doses of chemical aerosols inside every home
options.B: Clearing stagnant water pools around residential areas
options.C: Cutting away overgrown bushes near houses
options.D: Improving local waste disposal systems
